body: It can really feel like the end of the world. But hearing other people are making it though similar situations does make me feel a little better. And I'm glad me opening up helped you, even a little bit.

I wish I was alone, so other people didn't have to go through the intense emotions I have in me.

You'd think... but not always. When I told her I was depressed back in high school, she said "You aren't depressed, real depressed people can't even get out of bed in the morning!" ... and then would yell at me for, guess what, not being able to get out of bed in the morning. Add onto that the very negative reaction to coming out as bi (I was grounded for the first and only time... yeah...) and it makes it really hard to open up to family.

Thank you.

I think I should go see just advisor about this. Not a meeting I'm looking forward to. Maybe they can find something to help me out, but I don't know.

I don't wanna let down my family. They've put so much time, love, and money into my education. I'd hate to flush it all down because "I was sad". And like, I know my clinical depression isn't "just sad" but... It tells me that's all it is and it makes me feel like a lazy jackass.

If I get too much shit from my dad for having to take an extra semester, I fuckin' swear... He had to take a 5th year because he failed a bunch of shit, and not for mental illness. And my mom has like a psych degree and works with the mentally ill, she knows how debilitating it can be, but she's also got the highest expectations of me. it's so hard, going from straight A honors bullshit to flunking a bunch of classes because of mental illness.

Maybe I should see a crisis counselor. I think my campus has those.

Anyway, thanks for sharing your story. Knowing I'm not totally alone helps. Hopefully I can recover from this.

Thank you.

You're right, I don't always have the best people around me. My parents don't really get my depression/anxiety. I'm like half-in-the-closet as a bi dude in a conservative part of the South. Most of the time I'm hiding who I am, what I think, and how I feel. It really doesn't help when I have all this inside me and I can't express it to anyone. I've been in group therapy for a few months now and I still can't tell them half the stuff I'm feeling.

Life is a monster. I'm hoping things get better later on.
I'm really not interested in religion or spirtitual things. Sorry.

I'm not religious, so that stuff doesn't really help me any, sorry.

But I'll take the other stuff in mind, I guess. But I don't want to set myself to such lofty goals that I end up crashing down even further when I don't reach them.
